assessment: This study investigates development of the mechanosensory organ on Drosophila notum. It combines live imaging, mathematical modelling, genetics and behavioural analysis to show that, in the peripheral nervous system of Drosophila, entry of progenitor cells into mitosis is spatially and temporally controlled. The authors suggest that this ensures proper targeting of sensory neurons within the ventral nerve cord. This timing is important for axonogenesis and proper spatial arborization, ultimately influencing the animal's behaviour. The study will be of broad interest to those who work on the developmental of sense organs, and in general on the role of timing in development.
